chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: “Do you think that the bequeathing one from among us appoints whomever he wishes? No, by Allah. Rather, it is a covenant from Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله to one man after another, until the matter ends with its rightful possessor.”
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Minhal, from 'Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, similarly to it.

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the source of the covenant and appointment
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the matter or authority of Imamate
key_terms.الْمُوصِيَ: the one who makes the bequest or designation of succession
key_terms.رَسُولِهِ: His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, through whom the covenant is conveyed
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: its rightful possessor or designated holder
key_terms.عَهْدٌ: a binding covenant or divine pledge

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam appoint his successor by personal choice or by a covenant from Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the office of the Imam is not assigned by personal choice or preference. Rather, it is a divinely ordained covenant transmitted from one designated Imam to the next until it reaches its rightful holder. The report emphasizes the theological principle that Imamate is established by Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, not by human selection.
